_readme: GAME CONTENT: the battlefield obstacles (rocks, fallen rubble, broken pillar stumps, mossy boulders, a fallen bough) painted on each battle backdrop. One entry per (RegionId, ArtKey, Arena): RegionId a regions.json region, ArtKey the painted backdrop (a sprite's ArtKey in content/art/pixel/pixel-art-manifest.json, listed in content/data/Vfx/battle-art.json: backdrop/<region>/<backdrop id>/<arena>), Arena Small, Medium or Large, and Cells: the obstacle hexes as axial { Q, R } (HexGrid's coordinates, R < 0 the enemy side, R > 0 the player's). An obstacle blocks movement and standing only: nothing is deployed on it, walks onto or through it (paths go round it) or is knocked back onto it (a knockback stops at the last free hex, as at the board's edge); skills pass over it (there is no line of sight) and an area effect covers it harmlessly. Each battle fought in a region (EncounterSetup.RegionId) is fought on one of that region's layouts for its arena, picked from the battle's seed on its own stream (BattleLayouts.Pick: LootRoller.DeriveSeed(seed, 5) mod the number of layouts, in file order), so the battle, the balance simulator and the viewer, which draws that layout's backdrop, agree. A region and arena with no layout fights on the open board. Rules (BeastCraft.Encounters.ObstacleLayoutValidator, run on content load and by the tests): each ArtKey once; every cell on the board, once, in the neutral band (never in either deployment zone, so both sides deploy exactly as on an open board and every shape, template and boss still seats; the validator also re-packs every authored template on the obstructed board); Small 0-2 obstacles, Medium 2-5, Large 3-8; balanced-count fairness (enemy half against player half, and left against right of the vertical centre line, each within one); the free tiles one connected region. The painted backdrops show their obstacles on exactly these hexes (docs/art/hollow-art-slots.md; Tooling/ArtLab/scripts/layout_overlay.py draws them over any backdrop image for review). Obstacles change battles: after an edit, re-run the balance simulator (Tooling/BalanceSim/README.md), which samples r01's layouts for every PvE battle.
